correctness.rationale: For any nonzero finite-dimensional H1,H2 over the same real or complex scalar field and norm-one G, compactness of the unit spheres localizes near-norming x to E=ker(I-G*G) and near-norming pairs (x,y) for Re<Gx,y>→1 to y=Gx, x∈E. The exact formulas are p_G(T)=||T|E|| and ν_G(T)=w(U*P_F T|E), F=GE, U=G|E isometric. If F≠H2, a rank-one T with norming source e∈E and orthogonal output z∈Fperp has p_G=1 and ν_G=0. If F=H2, G vanishes on Eperp so GG*=I (and conversely); every A:E→E lifts to some T with p_G=||A|| and ν_G=w(A). Classical finite-dimensional Hilbert numerical indices then give index 1 if dim H2=1, 1/2 for complex coisometry with dim H2>=2, and 0 otherwise (real skew 2x2 witness, complex nilpotent witness). If dim H1>=dim H2>=2 complex, a coisometry can be approximated on the norm-one sphere by attenuating one, but not every, singular value, proving discontinuity exactly on coisometries. Independent 10000 complex unit-vector samples of 2x2 nilpotent lifted through 2x3 coisometry gave max radius ~0.499999996, compatible with sharp analytic 1/2. Finite samples do not certify universal theorem, which follows from Hilbert compression and polarization.

value.rationale: The relative numerical index is a natural already-defined operator geometric invariant; the complete real/complex and rectangular dimension trichotomy, exact coisometric positive case and discontinuity locus are specific useful classification statements. The sharp value and quotient interpretation distinguish it from routine restating the classical Hilbert index, especially for degenerate seminorms.

limitations: Not conventional full-norm G-index, which can have different values.
No general Banach-space extension or classification of all index-attaining T.
